scope: Proposition 3.4 (Information under angular separation) of the manuscript “Polynomial PEPS approximation of gapped square-grid ground states” (preprints/Polynomial-PEPS-approximation-of-gapped-square-grid-ground-states-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 265 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0b55ba0b87ad0468), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a > 0, A0 ≥ 1, an integer m0 ≥ 0, and p > 0. There is D < ∞ such that the following holds for all sufficiently large L. Let V be a set of at most m0 marked points in the plane, let X, E ⊆ Λ be disjoint, and let D log L ≤ n ≤ A0L, diam∞ X ≤ A0n. Put smin = D log L and dV(x) = minv∈V |x − v|∞, with d∅ = +∞. Suppose that for every x ∈ X, dist∞(x, E) ≥ a max{smin, min(n, dV(x))}. (3.18) Then IΩ(X : E) ≤ L−p . The constant D and the scale threshold are uniform in the marked points, physical sets, and Hamiltonian.
